title: Minimum Viable Product
hook: You don't need six more months of building. You need to find out if anyone actually wants this.
statement: Ship the smallest possible version that lets you start learning from real users.
explainer: An MVP isn't a small product. It's a cheap test. One online shoe store started by photographing shoes in local shops before buying any stock, just to see if people would order.
sop: Name the riskiest assumption your business rests on.
Decide what result would prove it wrong.
Build the smallest thing that gets you that result.
Put it in front of real users.
Use the data to pivot or keep going.
equation_example: 3 Hypotheses Tested over 6 weeks of Time-to-Build. 3 ÷ 6 = 0.5 hypotheses per week. Higher means your build time is turning into real learning fast. Lower means weeks of building with nothing you can actually test.
question: Write down the smallest thing you could ship this week that tests your riskiest assumption.
closing_statement: Learning is the product, not the shipped feature.
caption:
Principle Nº 287: Minimum Viable Product

You don't need six more months of building. You need to find out if anyone actually wants this.

Ship the smallest possible version that lets you start learning from real users.

Your turn: Write down the smallest thing you could ship this week that tests your riskiest assumption.
